cases.desc: The proposed work includes window replacement, restoration of the main entrance, facade repairs, and roof repairs. Window Replacement: The existing windows are aluminum IGU units installed in the 1990s, many of which have failed. The windows on the primary Grand Street south facade, plus one adjoining bay on each of the east and west elevations will be replaced with new double hung IGU wood windows with configurations and details to match the original 1886 design as determined by the review of archival photographs. The remainder of the windows on the secondary east, west and south facades will be replaced with new DH aluminum IGU windows, with configurations to match the original design. Entrance Restoration: The Grand Street entrance will be replaced with two new wood raised panel doors and new sidelites to match the original 1886 design. Facade Repairs: Local areas of spalled and cracked brick and brownstone masonry will be repaired with new matching face brick and appropriate crack filler materials and methodologies. Roof Repairs: The pyramidal roof slates on Grand Street exhibit numerous cracked and dislocated pieces and will be replaced in kind. The two lower asphaltic shingle gable roofs have also failed and will be replaced with new fiberglass roof shingles. New copper flashing, leaders and gutters will be restored to replace existing components that have exceeded their useful life.

cases.address: 218 1ST ST
cases.desc: We, the applicants, seek to renovate and expand the existing residential structure at Block 11402, Lot 21 within the Harsimus Cove Historic District. This proposal involves a strategic vertical and horizontal expansion that increases the Gross Building Area to 6,265 SF while strictly maintaining the currently permitted density of four dwelling units. The design is deeply rooted in the context of its immediate neighbors, seeking to harmonize with the historic street wall and overall fabric of the block. Notably, the project achieves a significant public benefit by reducing existing non-conforming lot coverage from 100% to 93%, thereby increasing permeable open space and improving local site drainage. The requested variances are necessitated by the unique practical constraints of the Harsimus Cove Historic District and are consistent with established neighborhood patterns:Front & Rear Setbacks (c variance): The 12 ft front setback is maintained to preserve the existing property line relationship, but its interaction with the horizontal expansion requires a rear yard of 22 ft. This is a "flexible c" variance justified by the neighborhood context: multiple properties on this specific block already maintain rear setbacks significantly below the 30 ft requirement. Aligning with these existing conditions allows for a building footprint that is consistent with the historic "street wall" and density of the adjacent structures. Building Height (c/d variance): The proposed height of 45.83 ft represents a modest 5.83 ft (approx. 14%) deviation from the 40 ft limit. This vertical expansion is critical to facilitating high-quality, family-sized housing (including 3 and 4-bedroom layouts) within the existing unit count. This avoids the "over-densification" of the neighborhood while providing modern, viable residential spaces. Negative Criteria & Public Good: The proposal satisfies the "negative criteria" as it imposes no substantial detriment to the public good. Rather, it advances the purposes of the Municipal Land Use Law (MLUL) by promoting a desirable visual environment, preserving a historic structure through adaptive reuse, and improving environmental site conditions via reduced lot coverage. Representation Disclosure: The applicants, Girish Shahdadpuri and Harish Pehlajani, are the individual owners of the subject property and are applying in their personal capacity rather than through a business entity (LLC or Corporation). In accordance with New Jersey Court Rule 1:21-1 and guidance provided by the Planning Department, we are exercising our right to represent ourselves pro se. While we have provided our own contact information in the attorney/representative fields to fulfill form requirements, we remain open to retaining counsel should the Board determine it necessary for this specific application.

cases.address: 218 1ST ST
cases.desc: The Owners seek to renovate and expand the existing residential structure at Block 11402, Lot 21 within the Harsimus Cove Historic District. This proposal involves a strategic vertical and horizontal expansion that increases the Gross Building Area to 6,265 SF while strictly maintaining the currently permitted density of four dwelling units. The design is deeply rooted in the context of its immediate neighbors, seeking to harmonize with the historic street wall and overall fabric of the block. Notably, the project achieves a significant public benefit by reducing existing non-conforming lot coverage from 100% to 93%, thereby increasing permeable open space and improving local site drainage. The requested variances are necessitated by the unique practical constraints of the Harsimus Cove Historic District and are consistent with established neighborhood patterns: Front & Rear Setbacks (c variance): The 12 ft front setback is maintained to preserve the existing property line relationship, but its interaction with the horizontal expansion requires a rear yard of 22 ft. This is a "flexible c" variance justified by the neighborhood context: multiple properties on this specific block already maintain rear setbacks significantly below the 30 ft requirement. Aligning with these existing conditions allows for a building footprint that is consistent with the historic "street wall" and density of the adjacent structures. Building Height (c/d variance): The proposed height of 45.83 ft represents a modest 5.83 ft (approx. 14%) deviation from the 40 ft limit. This vertical expansion is critical to facilitating high-quality, family-sized housing (including 3 and 4-bedroom layouts) within the existing unit count. This avoids the "over-densification" of the neighborhood while providing modern, viable residential spaces. Negative Criteria & Public Good: The proposal satisfies the "negative criteria" as it imposes no substantial detriment to the public good. Rather, it advances the purposes of the Municipal Land Use Law (MLUL) by promoting a desirable visual environment, preserving a historic structure through adaptive reuse, and improving environmental site conditions via reduced lot coverage. Representation Disclosure: The owners, Girish Shahdadpuri and Harish Pehlajani, are the individual owners of the subject property and are applying in their personal capacity rather than through a business entity (LLC or Corporation). In accordance with New Jersey Court Rule 1:21-1 and guidance provided by the Planning Department, we are exercising our right to represent ourselves pro se. While we have provided our own contact information in the attorney/representative fields to fulfill form requirements, we remain open to retaining counsel should the Board determine it necessary for this specific application.
